title: The 25 Best Goalkeepers in World Soccer—Ranked
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffJun 20, 2025David Raya is one of the best goalkeepers in the world. / Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside/Getty ImagesIf teams can’t score goals, matches can’t be won. And if teams can’t do that, trophies can’t be lifted and greatness can’t be achieved.
But what goes on further back on the pitch is equally as important, if not more so. In fact, in the modern era, a team’s identity and style is often defined by how good the goalkeeper is.

No longer is the role of the goalkeeper just to stop shots; it’s to provide quality distribution with both feet—both short and long—and have the ability to mop up behind a high line. Extreme levels of composure are required, as is a high level of technical ability and unflappable concentration levels.
It’s why the conversation of who the most exciting goalkeepers in the world are is such an exciting one.

The ranking is defined not only by recent form but contributions over a longer period of time, a player’s standing in the game and their overall reputation. It matters what level they are playing at (or have played at in a reasonable time frame) and how much they have personally impacted proceedings in the past. It also matters how much buzz they generate and how they perceived by supporters around the world.

Statistics are often used as the barometer for what good looks like, but we take into account the eye test as well. What players say in post-match interviews is a factor—you know, that classic line of questioning that is often put to a full back when they’ve taken on a pacy winger or when a center back is asked what it’s like to face a relentless goalscorer.
Trophies won, both at domestic and international level, is of course taken into account. There’s nothing better than playing in successful teams who know how to pick up silverware.

Como’s goalkeeper kept 19 clean sheets during 2025–26. / Image Photo Agency/Getty Images Como were as low as Serie D as recently as 2018–19, highlighting just how swift their rise has been.Fast forward the clock to 2026 and the Biancoblù had finished 4th in Serie A under the management of Cesc Fàbregas—an achievement so great that many of the top young players in the world have been enthused by the prospect of joining Como’s project.Jean Butez has more than played his part in Como’s success, blossoming into one of Italian soccer’s top goalkeepers. His 2025–26 campaign was particularly stellar, keeping 19 clean sheets and conceding just 28 times in 38 matches.

Uğurcan Çakır has been in fine form for Galatasaray. / Hakan Akgun/Anadolu/Getty ImagesIt was the end of an era when Fernando Muslera left Galatasaray in the summer of 2025. The Uruguay international had spent 14 years patrolling the posts in Istanbul, amassing 551 appearances, eight top-flight titles and even two goals. Replacing this larger-than-life figure was not a task for the faint hearted. Enter: Uğurcan Çakır.Plucked from rivals Trabzonspor for a record-breaking fee, Çakır has lived up to his billing as Türkiye’s most expensive goalkeeper ever. A towering character who has scarcely been fazed by the intimidating atmosphere of Rams Park, Çakır has performed the impossible: replacing Muslera.

Roefs has been an astute addition. / Lewis Storey/Getty ImagesRobin Roefs arrived at a Sunderland fresh from promotion with just one full season of senior action to his name. “He’s young, without a lot of experience,” Régis Le Bris would later admit. “Often you would say you need an experienced goalkeeper, because this role is really demanding, even psychologically.” But Roefs has proven more than up for the task.As commanding with his gloves as he is with his boots, the Dutch shot-stopper is imperative on both sides of the ball for Sunderland, snuffing out opposition attacks while spearing long passes forward to set up surges for his own side.Le Bris summed it up best: “He’s key.”

Vanja Milinkovic-Savić’s form led to Naples. /  Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesIt was Sergej this, Sergej that for so many years, but perhaps Vanja was the superior Milinkovic-Savić brother all along?O.K., that may be a slight exaggeration, but while Sergej is now away from mainstream prominence in the Saudi Pro League, Vanja has blossomed into one of Serie A’s best goalkeepers.The Serbian stalwart is a ruthless shot-stopper who has a penchant for saving penalties. After racking up continental-leading clean sheet figures at Torino, Milinkovic-Savić joined then-reigning champions Napoli, managed at the time by Antonio Conte—he’s someone who won’t try to sign you unless you’ve got something about you.

Matz Sels is an imposing figure. / Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty ImagesNottingham Forest struggled for continuity between the sticks after returning to the Premier League, with the likes of Dean Henderson and Keylor Navas earning minutes as the club’s No. 1.Forest’s cut-price addition of Matz Sels at the end of the January 2024 transfer window wasn’t regarded as a revolutionary bit of business, but the experienced Belgian proved he’s one of the smartest transfers of Evangelos Marinakis’s reign.The towering figure has an imposing backline ahead of him, but Sels’s impact cannot be overlooked. He earned a share of the Golden Glove with David Raya in 2024–25.

Yann Sommer’s aged like a fine wine in goal.  /  Isosport/MB Media/Getty Images Yann Sommer’s move to Inter didn’t raise many eyebrows because it was André Onana’s sale to Man Utd that grabbed the headlines. Yet the Swiss veteran proved a crucial cog in the club’s swift capture of the Serie A title.Sommer continued to perform at a high level for Inter and ended his three-year tenure with yet another title—this one under the stewardship of Cristian Chivu. He’s now at Club Brugge, where he’ll be targeting progress in the Champions League and the Belgian Pro League title.

Ivan Provedel has struggled for minutes at Inter. / Marco Canoniero/LightRocket/Getty ImagesThere was a story Ivan Provedel’s grandmother never tired of passing down to her grandson. When they lived in Russia, the legendary Lev Yashin was their neighbour. That connection to the greatest goalkeeper of all time wasn’t enough to initially persuade Provedel to pick up a pair of gloves.“I was a striker until I turned 15,” he would explain. “My goal-to-game ratio was actually decent.”Provedel’s scoring ratio now isn’t too bad now for a goalkeeper. The Lazio custodian has a one-in-eight record in the Champions League after netting a dramatic equalizer against Atlético Madrid in 2023.His more orthodox goalkeeping skills are also admirable, but a transfer from Lazio to Inter ahead of the 2026–27 season has stalled his career.

Gerónimo Rulli joined Manchester City last summer. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesGerónimo Rulli bounced around Europe after making his name at Real Sociedad, but looked to have really made a home for himself at Olympique Marseille.Quickly shown faith by Roberto De Zerbi, the Argentine blossomed in both Ligue 1 and the Champions League, giving Marseille the quality required to make steady progress under the Italian’s watch.Except a summer move to Manchester City has turned him into nothing more than a back-up, straining for limited minutes behind Gianluigi Donnarumma.It’s a similar story at the international level. Had Rulli been any other nationality other than Argentine, he may have earned more than the meagre nine international caps currently attached to his name. But don’t let those numbers fool you into thinking he’s not a quality operator.

Pickford had another clean sheet-heavy Premier League season. / IMAGO/PPAUKDespite spending much of his Premier League career as a meme, Jordan Pickford has undergone quite the redemption arc in recent years.He’s quietly become more reliable and remains as useful as ever in possession, while he was one of the top players at Euro 2020 and would have become a national hero had that final shootout ended in an England win. There wasn’t much he could do to deny Spain Euro 2024 glory as he enjoyed another successful individual tournament, before he was largely let down by a makeshift backline and Thomas Tuchel’s conservative tactics at the 2026 World Cup.  Everton have flirted with relegation from the Premier League in recent times, but Pickford has consistently dragged the Toffees away from danger and is finally playing for a side now capable of challenging at the other end of the table.

Diogo Costa has been linked with Europe’s elite. / IMAGO/Maciej RogowskiThe archetypal modern goalkeeper: Diogo Costa is as good with his feet as he is with his hands. Porto’s homegrown skipper is even better at penalties.Rather than rely upon reams of data and video analysis, Costa has put his ridiculous record at saving efforts from 12 yards down to gut feeling. “It’s about instinct, about having the nose for it, about feeling what a player is going to do,” he once said.

Lammens has enjoyed a steady start. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesSir Alex Ferguson knows a good goalkeeper when he sees one. After suffering through a drought of top-quality shot-stoppers in between Peter Schmeichel and Edwin van der Sar, he also knows what a not-so-good one looks like. Senne Lammens has the golden seal of approval.“The goalkeeper has been outstanding,” Ferguson gushed after Lammens enjoyed a confident start to life between the posts for Manchester United last season.Entirely unburdened by the weight of expectation which comes with playing for the world’s most scrutinized football club, the springy Belgian made a mockery of then-manager Ruben Amorim’s pre-arrival warning that proclaimed “it’s hard to be a Manchester United goalkeeper in this moment.”But the statement from Amorim is ringing more true one year later at Old Trafford.

Manuel Neuer is still going strong in his 20th season as a professional. / Shaun Botterill/Getty ImagesManuel Neuer played a transformative role in the reinvention of the modern goalkeeper and, despite being over 40, remains one of the best sweeper-keepers in the business.Neuer is nearing the end of his illustrious career but continues to sparkle for Bayern Munich, fending off a number of challengers to remain the man to beat between the posts.
